Code-first starts from classes and mapping. Database-first starts from an existing schema. Both can use EF Core; choose the workflow that matches who controls the database.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Code-first workflow

dotnet ef migrations add AddCourse
dotnet ef database update

Add a property to the entity, generate a migration, inspect its SQL and data-loss risks, then apply it in a training database. Keep migrations in source control. Do not delete a migration already applied to a shared environment just to hide a mistake.

Database-first workflow

dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold "Name=ConnectionStrings:School" Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer --context SchoolDb --output-dir GeneratedModels --no-onconfiguring

Configure the named connection for the project first. The command reads schema and generates entity/context code. Use a clean separate project for this exercise so it does not duplicate the existing SchoolDb. Put custom logic in separate/partial files; regeneration can overwrite generated files. Do not hard-code credentials in generated code.

Compare carefully

Code-first is convenient when your team owns the schema and wants reviewed migrations. Database-first is convenient for a supplied or centrally managed schema. Neither approach removes the need for keys, constraints, backups, indexes or careful migration review. Expected scaffold output is a context plus entity classes matching the database’s tables, not a finished UI.

Try it yourself

A scaffold command creates a duplicate SchoolDb. Fix it.

Worked answer

Run the example in a clean project or choose a distinct context/namespace and remove conflicting generated definitions intentionally.

Does database-first mean CRUD must use raw SQL?

Worked answer

No. Generated entities and a context can use ordinary EF queries and SaveChanges.
